gloss: calling at a port; port of call

definitions.gloss: calling at a port; making a port call; stopping at a port
definitions.explanation: When a ship stops at a port during a voyage, either for refueling, loading cargo, or allowing passengers to disembark temporarily.

examples.japanese: {次|つぎ}の{寄港地|きこうち}は{神戸|こうべ}です。
examples.english: The next port of call is Kobe.

examples.japanese: クルーズ{船|せん}が{横浜|よこはま}{港|こう}に{寄港|きこう}した。
examples.english: A cruise ship called at the port of Yokohama.

examples.japanese: この{航路|こうろ}は{途中|とちゅう}{三|みっ}つの{港|みなと}に{寄港|きこう}しながら{目的地|もくてきち}に{向|む}かう。
examples.english: This route heads to the destination while calling at three ports along the way.

notes:
Used specifically for ships stopping at ports. Not used for aircraft or other vehicles. Used as a noun or suru-verb ({寄港|きこう}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {寄港地|きこうち}: port of call
- {寄港|きこう}する: to call at a port
- {寄港|きこう}を{予定|よてい}する: to be scheduled to call at a port
- {緊急|きんきゅう}{寄港|きこう}: emergency port call

WATCH OUT:
Several words share the reading きこう:
- {気候|きこう}: climate
- {機構|きこう}: mechanism, organization
- {寄稿|きこう}: contributing an article
- {紀行|きこう}: travelogue

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {入港|にゅうこう}: entering a port — arriving at the final destination port
- {出港|しゅっこう}: leaving port — departing from a port
- {寄港|きこう}: a temporary stop at a port during a voyage
